title: Autonomy and PNT conformance and test-and-evaluation tooling: machine-to-machine conformance suites for MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/FANTOM-style interfaces, DDIL scenario replay, and an ASPN synthetic-measurement generator with pntOS plug-in conformance checks scored against the DHS Resilient PNT framework
problem: Vendors that must plug into government autonomy and PNT reference interfaces, and the lab staff who assess them, prove conformance and degraded-environment behavior only at capacity-limited government events and live tests, because no affordable, vendor-neutral software harness exists for the open subset of those interfaces.

user.exact_role: Integration and test engineer at a small autonomy or alternative-PNT vendor preparing for a government assessment event, SBIR Phase I/II deliverable or milestone NAVWAR-compliance review; secondarily a government lab T&E engineer (SOFWERX/PEO-SDA UxSAI, C5ISR Center PNT, PMS 406) who runs vendor software through scenario sets
organization_examples: Drone Dominance and Blue UAS Framework component vendors (MAVLink/PX4-based)
USV/UUV autonomy vendors implementing UMAA services
Alt-PNT sensor vendors (DIU TQS cohort, MagNav, vision-nav, LEO-PNT) writing pntOS plug-ins
Army C5ISR Center PNT and PM PNT test engineers
Civil timing operators (telecom, utilities) buying under CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance

current_workflow: 1. Vendor obtains the interface specification: MAVLink and PX4 (public), UMAA ICDs (AUVSI, registration), ASPN-ICD YAML and pntOS-C API (public GitHub), STANAG 4586 (NATO-controlled document, obtained via program or national standards office), FANTOM Core M2M API (government-controlled, program access only).
2. Vendor writes the adapter or plug-in and tests it against ad hoc scripts, a vendor HIL rig, or (for PNT) an RF simulator (Spirent, Safran Skydel) if it can afford one.
3. Vendor waits for a government slot: SOFWERX assessment event, PNTAX/APEX, CCA/A-GRA phase, PMS 406 lab, or SBIR Phase I demonstration.
4. Government staff run the vendor's software through their own scenario sets and government M&S (MDQDA, GIANT/CIGNM, program simulators) and report defects late.
5. For PNT-using programs, the milestone decision authority demands NAVWAR-compliance evidence (DoDI 4650.08); the evidence table is assembled manually per program.
6. Repeat per software drop, per program and per interface family.
current_solution: Government-furnished compliance test tools for Army UAS/IOP and STANAG 4586 (Army states such tools are available to programs and eligible vendors); MITRE UMAA reference implementation (RECALL - not re-verified this session); vendor-specific HIL rigs; Spirent PNT X/PNT Xe and Safran Skydel (RF-level GNSS scenario simulators with Python automation) for PNT; Applied Intuition's simulation and validation tooling and the CDAO 'Autonomy Factory' for enterprise autonomy validation; government-run assessment events (SOFWERX UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems AE and Synthetic Data Modeler AE, 2026); annual PNTAX; for civil PNT, vendor self-attestation against the DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 with no certification body.
failure: Conformance and degraded-mode behavior are validated only at the government's cadence and inside its tooling, so vendors discover integration failures late and cannot reproduce them; alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' than GNSS models and engagement-level trade tools 'do not yet exist' (GAO-21-320SP); civil resilience-level claims are self-declared and single-number resilience scores have been shown to be decision-unstable under framework-aligned weighting (arXiv 2607.05415, July 2026) - so there is no trusted independent yardstick. But the failure is one of capacity and cadence, not absence of tooling: the government and its consortia already own or plan the tools for each interface family.

evidence.claim: Army planned a compliance toolkit to auto-verify pntOS plug-ins; alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' than GNSS models; the ability to model multiple integrated technologies 'does not yet exist'; SOF are 'reluctant to accept modeling and simulation results'; field tests require shutting down civil airspace; DoD MOSA-PNT initiative funded at $17M FY2020-2024.
evidence.source_title: GAO-21-320SP, Defense Navigation Capabilities: DOD is Developing Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Technologies to Complement GPS
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: NAVWAR compliance must be determined and reported at each acquisition milestone with T&E plans sufficient to validate it - structural, recurring demand for compliance evidence.
evidence.source_title: DoDI 4650.08 Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) and Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR), Change 1
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Navy NAVWAR open topic NP004 accepts synthetic ASPN/pntOS data for Phase I and states 'innovation required on the ingestion of disparate types' - the one concrete government acceptance of synthetic ASPN streams as SBIR-grade input (topic closed 2026-09-23).
evidence.source_title: Navy SBIR 26.5 DON26BX05-NP004 topic and Q&A
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SOFWERX with PEO-SDA ran a UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler Assessment Event (milestones June-October 2026) to select synthetic-data generation for EO/IR computer-vision model development, and a separate UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Event (whitepapers, downselect, government-run T&E). The synthetic-data buy is CV imagery, not interface conformance or scenario replay; T&E is performed by the government.
evidence.source_title: sam.gov: UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler Assessment Event (AE); Soldier Systems Daily: SOFWERX UxSAI Mission Autonomy Systems Assessment Event; DefenseScoop: SOCOM planning to test new mission autonomy software

evidence.claim: Army UAS interoperability program states that 'many software test tools are available to programs and eligible vendors to help demonstrate compliance with applicable standards, and these test tools continue to evolve to further automate compliance testing' (STANAG 4586-based IOP messages) - the STANAG 4586/IOP conformance slot is served by government-furnished tooling.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ISTO announced the PNT Standards Consortium, founded by Leidos, IS4S and TRX Systems, to govern pntOS and ASPN through an open consensus process - the natural home for an official (free) conformance suite; IS4S markets pntOS commercially.
evidence.source_title: ISTO Announces Formation of PNT Standards Consortium to Unify Open Navigation Standards (GlobeNewswire via Manila Times); pntstandards.org; is4s.com/pntos
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: RF-level PNT scenario incumbents keep moving down-market and toward automation: Spirent (now Keysight) launched PNT Xe to extend GNSS simulation 'to more users across the development lifecycle' (Nov 2025); Safran launched Skydel AI, which configures scenarios via natural language by generating Python code (ION GNSS+ Sept 2025). Neither result mentions ASPN message output - public evidence insufficient on ASPN support.
evidence.source_title: Spirent press release; Safran Navigation & Timing: Skydel AI
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 defines resilience Levels 0-4 with Prevent/Respond/Recover behaviors; CISA's Federal PNT Services Acquisitions guidance (March 2024) directs federal buyers to specify resilience expectations; the results show vendors (Oscilloquartz/ADVA, VIAVI) self-declare conformance and no certification or accredited test body appears - so demand for independent scoring is latent, not funded.
evidence.source_title: DHS S&T Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0; CISA Federal PNT Services Acquisitions Guidance; VIAVI press release
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: A July 2026 arXiv study finds single-number PNT resilience ratings are decision-unstable under framework-aligned weighting - i.e., the 'score against the DHS framework' output this gap proposes is scientifically contested as a ranking instrument.
evidence.source_title: How Stable Is a PNT Resilience Score? Decision-Instability of Single-Number Resilience Ratings under Framework-Aligned Weighting (arXiv 2607.05415)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DIU established third-party 'Recognized Assessors' (as of Sept 2025) to perform standardized assessments of drone platforms and components against the Blue UAS standard (NDAA/cybersecurity), delivering reports to DIU for a certification decision - DoD does outsource compliance assessment to third parties, but for supply-chain/cyber compliance, not interface conformance, and to accredited organizations.
evidence.source_title: DIU: seeking recognized assessors to support Blue UAS NDAA compliance; Mobilicom Blue UAS Framework overview
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: SOCOM requires vendors to integrate flight controllers with government-owned FANTOM Core via M2M API and/or BMS - the FANTOM-style interface is government-controlled and reachable only inside a program.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CDAO selected Applied Intuition to underpin a DoD-wide 'Autonomy Factory' shared environment to develop, validate and certify autonomous systems (announced 2026-05-14; CDAO production contract ceiling up to $171.1M over three years reported 2025-01-14; ceiling is not obligations, production status unverified). Public evidence insufficient on whether it covers PNT/pntOS conformance.

evidence.claim: Academic search-based UAS testing frameworks are validated only in nominal and fault edge cases, not jamming, DDIL or sensor denial - degraded-environment replay remains an open T&E problem in the literature.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because the customers are also the toolmakers. Each interface family already has an owner that furnishes or plans free tooling: Army PM UAS furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP compliance test tools to programs and eligible vendors (army.mil), MITRE supports UMAA compliance (RECALL - not re-verified), the Army planned an automatic pntOS plug-in compliance toolkit in 2021 (GAO-21-320SP) and the pntOS/ASPN authors now govern the standards through the ISTO consortium (2026-06), SOCOM runs its own UxSAI assessment events and buys CV synthetic data rather than interface tooling (2026), and CDAO has selected Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation. Tangram Flex (Dayton, ~$11M 2024 revenue per company index, RECALL) already sells interface-code generation and verification to USAF programs, which shows the slot supports a services-heavy small business rather than a venture. On the PNT side, RF simulator incumbents (Spirent, Safran Skydel) own the scenario-generation budget, and civil DHS-framework conformance is self-attested with no certifying body, so nobody pays for an independent score.
technical_wedge: The only piece a startup could plausibly own is a software-only, message-level (not RF-level) degraded-PNT scenario generator that emits ASPN-2023 measurement streams (GNSS, IMU, clock, magnetometer, RF-ranging) under scripted jamming, spoofing, multipath and dropout profiles, plus a CI runner that executes a vendor's pntOS-C plug-in against those streams and produces a schema-conformance report, a Resilient-PNT-Framework behavior checklist (Prevent/Respond/Recover per level, reported as pass/fail behaviors rather than a single score) and a draft DoDI 4650.08 evidence table. A MAVLink/PX4 DDIL replay harness (link-loss, latency, GNSS-loss injection into SITL) is a natural second module. UMAA over DDS is feasible from public ICDs; STANAG 4586 and FANTOM Core are out of reach without program access and are excluded from the wedge.

mvp.what: Open-core 'PNT interface digital twin': ASPN-2023 synthetic-measurement generator with degradation profiles grounded in public datasets (TEXBAT spoofing scenarios, public MagNav flight data - RECALL, not re-verified), a pntOS-C plug-in CI runner, and a report generator (schema conformance, RPCF behavior checklist, NAVWAR evidence table); plus a PX4 SITL DDIL replay module.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the open subset: run the public pntOS-C example plug-in and two open-source estimators through ten scripted degradation scenarios in CI and emit the reports; show a PX4 SITL mission replayed under link-loss and GNSS-loss profiles with pass/fail against declared behaviors.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That harness findings reproduce real integration failures on at least two real vendors' pntOS plug-ins under NDA; that a NAVWAR/PM PNT or SBIR reviewer accepts the synthetic streams and evidence table as milestone-grade input (NP004 Q&A is the only public precedent); and that a vendor will pay $25k-$100k for it rather than wait for the consortium's free suite.

data_requirement.what: Public interface specifications (ASPN-ICD YAML, pntOS-C API, MAVLink XML, UMAA ICDs), public GNSS spoofing/jamming datasets to calibrate degradation profiles, realistic sensor error models for alternative PNT sources, and - for credibility - real vendor plug-ins and logs under NDA.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Public specs and datasets: yes, unclassified and Distribution A. Realistic alt-PNT error models: partly (published literature; the government's own models are internal and GAO says fidelity is poor). Vendor plug-ins/logs: only by partnership and NDA. STANAG 4586 document: NATO-controlled, obtainable via a program or national body - likely not for a non-U.S.-person founder without counsel. FANTOM Core API and A-GRA: government-controlled, program access only.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by U.S. citizens or permanent residents and U.S. location (13 CFR 121.702); today neither founder qualifies, so SBIR is closed until the German founder holds a green card and the Indonesian founder's stake plus any investor stake stays under 50% - model this before any priced round (GAO-24-107004 notes VC-majority eligibility is agency-elective). SOFWERX assessment events typically restrict to U.S. companies and may involve CUI/ITAR (public evidence insufficient on the specific UxSAI events' eligibility). Vendor-paid pilots and civil work carry no such barrier. Needs counsel.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, and most do not need to: Applied Intuition already sells validation tooling and holds the CDAO enterprise slot; Anduril and Shield AI run internal A-GRA/Lattice test rigs; Spirent/Safran can add ASPN export in one release; the consortium can publish a free suite; Tangram Flex already sells interface verification. A six-month response is realistic for any of them if the market proved real.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a venture. The startup's only structural advantage is vendor-neutrality (no CCA competitor can be the arbiter), but the government and the standards consortium are more neutral still and price at zero. The residual is a services-heavy devtools niche or an acqui-hire into IS4S/Leidos/Applied Intuition/Tangram Flex.

capital_required.assumptions: INFERENCE/LOW. PoC = two founders for 6 months on the open subset plus cloud CI. Credible demo adds one senior navigation/estimation engineer (12 months), two vendor pilots under NDA, and legal counsel on export classification. 'Production deployment' here means a government lab or consortium adopting the runner as reference plus a paid OTA to integrate with its M&S - which additionally requires U.S.-person staff and CUI handling (CMMC L2), and likely program access that this team lacks.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The open-subset harness (public ASPN/pntOS-C, MAVLink, UMAA ICDs, DHS framework) can plausibly be built as unclassified, publicly available software; no ATO is needed for vendor-side CI tooling. Burden rises sharply when the tool is adapted to military-controlled interfaces (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core, A-GRA), touches vendor CUI logs (CMMC Level 2), or is used inside a government lab (ATO, U.S.-person staff). Whether test tooling 'specially designed' for military autonomy interfaces is ITAR technical data is a counsel question, not a judgment made here.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian co-founder can work on the public-standards core and the civil DHS-RPCF product; access to STANAG 4586 documents, FANTOM Core APIs, vendor CUI logs and any SOFWERX/program engagement would need a deemed-export and CUI review by counsel and may be foreclosed. SBIR is closed to the current cap table regardless. Describe constraints; do not treat as a legal determination.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The PNT half has a real civil twin (DHS RPCF v2.0, NIST IR 8323r1, CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance March 2024, IEEE P1952 - RECALL) and civil timing vendors already market conformance, but conformance is self-attested with no certifying body or mandate, so a paying civil buyer for independent scoring is a HYPOTHESIS. MAVLink/PX4 replay has some commercial drone-QA demand but is served by open-source SITL tooling and vendor CI.

defensibility.explanation: Scenario libraries and degradation profiles could become a modest asset, and consortium standing plus a lab's adoption of the runner as reference would be the real moat - but standards are open, the government and consortium can publish free suites, RF-simulator incumbents can replicate degradation profiles, and the scoring output is scientifically contested (arXiv 2607.05415). No data, accreditation or network-effect moat is visible.

why_now: 2025-2026 moved reference interfaces from paper to practice: ASPN-ICD (2026-01) and pntOS-C (2026-04) went public, the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium formed (2026-06), SOCOM mandated FANTOM Core in solicitations (2026-06) and stood up UxSAI assessment events (2026-08), first A-GRA validation flights occurred (2026-02), NAVWAR accepted synthetic ASPN data as SBIR input (2026-08), DIU created third-party Blue UAS assessors (2025-09), and GPS-denied operation became routine (dozen-plus monthly domestic interference tests per NAVCEN). The counter-signal is equally recent: the same period saw the government and consortium claim the tooling role for themselves.
killer_risk: There is no requirement owner and no budget for third-party conformance tooling because every interface owner furnishes or plans its own free tools (Army STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, planned pntOS toolkit, ISTO consortium, MITRE UMAA, SOCOM's own assessment pipeline, CDAO's Applied Intuition environment), so the paid market collapses to a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap - a consultancy or acqui-hire outcome, not a company that justifies $2-5M, and the civil 'score against the DHS framework' output has no certifying customer and is scientifically contested.

allied_extension: Marginally more compelling on the autonomy side: UK/Australia/Japan are converging on shared uncrewed C2 software via AUKUS Maritime Big Play (2025-08) and STANAG 4586 is a NATO standard, so a conformance harness could in principle serve allied navies and drone makers (e.g., European vendors needing STANAG 4586/FMN gateways). But STANAG 4586 access is nationally controlled, allied programs also rely on primes and government labs, and ASPN/pntOS adoption outside the U.S. is unproven (3 stars/4 forks on pntOS-C as of 2026-08-26). Allies do not change the no-budget-owner problem.
